ai_summary: Great Britain is currently generating 14.2 GW of wind power, with Scotland delivering an estimated Scottish wind output of 3.5 GW, representing 34.7% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This strong renewable performance has driven Scottish carbon intensity down to 0 gCO2/kWh versus 59 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. Despite this green milestone, transmission boundary limits prevent clean energy from flowing south to major demand centers. As a result, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 19.1 GWh, incurring an immediate constraint cost of about £392,541. To replace this lost clean volume, fossil generation was dispatched down south, resulting in an estimated 3,628,886 m3 of gas burned elsewhere and producing an additional 6,685 tonnes of CO2. Annualizing this daily balancing expense indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £143 million. Socialized across national electricity consumption through system balancing mechanisms, this reflects an estimated increase of roughly £0.5/MWh on everybody's invoice in the UK. Upgrading cross-border network capacity remains essential to preventing carbon leakage, easing consumer balancing surcharges, and fully utilizing Scotland's clean power potential.
